title: Refactor SSO compatibility shims into unified identity adapter; apply OpenSSL/JWT remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We have accumulated multiple small SSO adapter shims across services (auth-proxy, console-api, and private-deploy agent) that each perform slightly different token validation and OpenSSL usage patterns. Recent CVE disclosures and customer reports of intermittent SAML assertion failures revealed inconsistent library versions and duplicated compatibility code. This ticket consolidates the shims into a single, tested identity adapter library and performs coordinated upgrades/pin-and-patch to OpenSSL, the JWT/OAuth libraries, and the SAML dependency stack.
acceptance_criteria: A single internal package (redwood-identity-adapter) used by auth-proxy, console-api, and private-agent replaces per-service shims
All services compile and pass CI with pinned OpenSSL 3.1.x minor with security patches applied
JWT/OAuth library upgraded to latest stable with breaking-change shim where necessary (no production behavior regressions observed in canary)
SAML adapter updated and test vectors for common IdPs (Okta, AzureAD, OneLogin) pass
Regression test suite (integration+fuzz) shows no increase in assertion/validation failures compared to baseline
Security review completed and signoff attached, release notes listing CVEs/patches included
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): Build redwood-identity-adapter and replace internal imports in auth-proxy branch. Run unit tests and new integration harness locally
Phase 2 (staging canary): Deploy updated auth-proxy+console-api to staging-canary with feature flag identity_adapter=true; monitor SAML/JWT error rate for 72h
Phase 3 (gradual prod): Enable on 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% in 24-48h windows, keep automated rollback on error-rate spike
Phase 4 (agents & Dedicated): Ship private-agent and dedicated pool upgrades with coordination docs for on-prem customers who pin dependencies
Hotfix window: Prepare backout PRs and previous-version builds for immediate rollback
testing_plan: Unit test coverage >= 90% for adapter boundary logic
Integration tests simulating Okta/Azure/OneLogin SAML flows (assertion time skew, audience mismatches, encrypted assertions)
Fuzz token parsing and malformed JWT inputs; ensure no panics and graceful errors
Chaos tests: simulate slow OpenSSL engine initialization and dropped connections
Performance bench: compare auth latency before/after for common token sizes (median and P99)
Security scan of resulting binary for known CVEs and transitive dependencies
risks_mitigation: Risk: Behavior drift due to JWT library change. Mitigation: compatibility shim and test vectors; keep previous parser as fallback behind flag
Risk: OpenSSL ABI differences on older customer hosts. Mitigation: bundle statically for private-agent builds where required and document minimal distro requirements
Risk: SAML assertion edge cases break specific IdPs. Mitigation: collect failing assertion payloads in staging, add targeted tests, and coordinate with affected customers
Risk: Rollout causes increased latency. Mitigation: benchmark and add circuit-breaker fallback to older auth-proxy at runtime
